To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most energy efficient routing protocols belong to the Network Structure category, while the most energy efficient protocols in each category are: (i) in the Network Structure category: LEACH, (ii) in the Communication Model category: MTE, (iii) in the Topology Based category: MECN, and (iv) in the Reliable Routing category: QoS-based protocols.

the most energy efficient protocols are those that use a combination of hierarchical and location-based routing, while the most energy efficient hierarchical protocols use a combination of clustering and data aggregation.

(a) Network Structure based routing schemes are the most popular schemes, (b) The majority of the routing schemes are hierarchical, (c) The majority of them are Query-based and (d) The majority of location-based routing schemes are based on the location information of the source node.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) the classification of energy efficient routing protocols in WSNs; (b) a detailed analysis and evaluation of the energy efficient routing protocols; (c) a comparison of the proposed protocols with each other, in terms of energy efficiency, network lifetime and scalability; (d) a discussion on the open issues in energy efficient routing for WSNs.
the following questions: (i) What is the classification of the energy efficient routing protocols?
the surveying of energy-efficient routing protocols for WNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single routing protocol which can satisfy all the requirements of WSNs.
the routing protocols proposed for WSN, are not energy-efficient enough and more research is needed in this area.
the energy efficiency of routing protocols for WNSs is a very important issue, and many researchers have been focusing their efforts on the development of efficient energy saving routing protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have classified the routing protocols for WNSs in four categories, we have analyzed the energy efficient routing protocols, we have classified the energy efficient routing schemes in four main categories and we have analyzed all the energy efficient routing proposals since 2004.
we have provided a survey on energy efficient protocols for WSN, we have classified them and we have described their energy efficiency issues.
we have presented an overview of the most important energy-efficient routing protocols proposed for wireless sensor networks, and we have provided a classification for them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed protocols can be classified according to the operations that are responsible for energy consumption.
there is a need of a new classification scheme, which will be able to cover all the issues and operations of each protocol.

, in order to design a routing protocol that will be energy efficient for WSN applications, one has to take into account the following issues: the network topology, the network size, the number of the sensors, the network's lifetime, the energy consumption of sensors, the energy consumption for communication, the communication range of sensors, the data aggregation, the data fusion, the data dissemination, the mobility of sensors, the mobility of sink, the data reliability, the QoS requirements and the security issues.
